Proves the zone matters even for a `date`-typed field, where no instant is ever constructed — the zone decides which calendar day "now" falls on, and therefore which week/month/quarter/year the preset resolves to. The pinned `now` is `2026-08-16T23:30:00Z`, a Sunday in UTC but already Monday 2026-08-17T01:30 in `Europe/Paris`.

The consequence is deliberately dramatic rather than subtle: resolved in Paris, `thisWeek` is the week starting Monday 2026-08-17, i.e. `[2026-08-17, 2026-08-24)`. Resolved in UTC, "today" would still be Sunday 2026-08-16, which (with the Monday-start policy) belongs to the PREVIOUS week — `[2026-08-10, 2026-08-17)`, a range that does not overlap the correct one by a single day. An implementation that treats the zone as relevant only to `datetime` fields fails this case and passes case 003, which is why both exist. Both bounds are `dateValue`s, since `hireDate` is declared `date`.
